title: When there is no refinement the name of the attribute stays in the URL
body:
Where there is no refinement the attribute stays in the URL.

![attr-url](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/393765/18548383/adc13c80-7b48-11e6-9650-ddacf9e0cc8b.gif)

comments.body: Let's say you set the default value of a `RefinementList` on the `"animals"` facet to `["cats"]`. When you first load the page, this default value won't be shown in the URL. The only way to deselect the `"cats"` value in this case is to explicitly set the `"animals"` facet value to an empty array. Just removing the entire facet value won't do, because then the default value will be selected again.
Ok got it, thanks @Morhaus. So one thing we could do, is actually building the query without the facets that have an empty string value.

> The only way to deselect the "cats" value in this case is to explicitly set the "animals" facet value to an empty array

@mthuret In any way, we just need to keep this behavior, since it's feasible for people to do so, it's a feature (not just a weird edge case)
